mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 2.5% for two consecutive months signals the Federal Reserve's loss of control, prompting preemptive equity reallocation and driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.5 and remains > 2.5 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) during inflation spikes above 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 140,000 new jobs monthly indicates labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth and pushes 20-day S&P 500 returns into positive territory.
failure_condition: During the trigger period, SPX 20-day returns are negative or flat in 80% of instances (rolling IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling below 100) suggests weakening manufacturing momentum, which typically precedes equity drawdowns; this should be associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
regime_hint: early-cycle soft landing turning into contraction
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the IC between INDPRO and SPX 20d returns remains positive (>0.05) despite INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising home sales (HOUST > 1,000) reflect resilient consumer demand, which accelerates corporate investment plans and yields positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: During trigger windows, 60-day returns are negative in more than 70% of cases (rolling IC < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RSAFS above 450 million dollars signals excess liquidity chasing safe assets, which can precede equity risk-on flows and push 20-day SPX returns into positive territory.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS crosses above 450 and remains > 450 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During RSAFS > 450 periods, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 5% over three months indicates weaker wage growth pressures, which often coincides with equity risk aversion and negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During UNRATE < 5% periods, 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (rolling IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in GDPC1 (real GDP momentum) below trend suggests economic softness that precedes equity market compression and negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60-day windows during GDPC1 declines, 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both HOUST and PAYEMS above their respective 1,000 and 140,000 thresholds for two consecutive months signals robust consumer and labor demand, which amplifies equity risk-on sentiment and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1,000 AND PAYEMS > 140,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During co-occurrence of both triggers, 20-day returns are negative in > 75% of windows (rolling IC < -0.15).
